claims.text: A nanostructured catalyst with a hierarchical microstructure architecture will exhibit enhanced HER catalytic activity under electrochemical conditions.
A nanostructured catalyst with a hierarchical microstructure architecture will exhibit enhanced HOR catalytic activity under electrochemical conditions.
A nanostructured catalyst with a hierarchical microstructure architecture will have greater durability under HER and HOR electrochemical conditions.
Controlled design and synthesis can produce a hierarchical microstructure with optimized pore size and pore distribution.
Optimized pore size and distribution reduce diffusion limitations.
The hierarchical microstructure increases catalyst surface area.
The hierarchical microstructure protects the catalyst from degradation.
Reduced diffusion limitations and increased surface area enhance mass transport and reaction kinetics.
Protection from degradation enhances catalyst durability.
The nanostructured catalyst is predicted to provide a 20% increase in catalytic activity relative to the average performance of traditional catalysts.
The nanostructured catalyst is predicted to provide a 30% increase in durability relative to the average performance of traditional catalysts.
Preliminary experiments provide a basis for the predicted activity and durability improvements.
A potential range of -1.0 V to 1.0 V versus RHE encompasses typical HER and HOR operating potentials.
Synthesis inconsistencies, electrolyte variations, and testing conditions may cause variation in catalyst performance.
Traditional catalysts with non-optimized microstructure architecture provide an appropriate performance baseline.
